newsitem.title: USA: Texas tries to block Ku Klux Klan propaganda win.
newsitem.headline: Texas tries to block Ku Klux Klan propaganda win.

text.p: Texas has gone to court to block a Ku Klux Klan faction from winning propaganda points by joining an "adopt-a-highway" anti-litter programme, officials said on Tuesday.
The United Knights of the Ku Klux Klan have applied for inclusion in the statewide programme, offering to clean up two separate two-mile (3.2 km) stretches of highway north of Fort Worth.
If accepted, the group would be entitled to put up road signs commemorating its clean-up efforts.

Texas Attorney General Dan Morales filed papers before a federal court on Monday, requesting a declaratory judgment stating the state's Department of Transportation is not required to allow the Ku Klux Klan group's participation.
He argued the programme is open only to civic and non-profit groups, private businesses and family organisations.
"This adopt-a-highway programme is for respectable citizens and civic organisations. The Ku Klux Klan is not a respectable civic organisation," Morales' spokesman Ron Dusek said.
"It would be disgraceful and insulting to all of those who have suffered at the hands of the Ku Klux Klan, which is a violent and criminal organisation," he told Reuters.
But Joe Earl Allcock, the Klan group's Imperial Wizard, said his faction rejected violence and only wanted to help clean up roadside litter.

"I was born and raised here in Fort Worth and every day I see what it looks like on the side of the road and it's trashy," Allcock, a rodeo clown, told the Fort Worth Star-Telegram. "And we want to clean it up."

Dusek said state officials successfully blocked a previous attempt by another Klan group to adopt a highway when it went to the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. Missouri won a similar case, but a Klan group in Arkansas forced state authorities there to allow its participation.
"Eventually, this may wind up with the Supreme Court," Duske said. "We hope not, we think it's a very cut and dried situation."
